messages:
maria (PM): Quick sync: customer requested tenant-prefetch + integrated generator for the cadence initiative. We need scope locked by EOD Friday. Primary goals: 99th <250ms for short completions, clear tenant isolation, and a canary rollout w/ rollback criteria.

aj (EngLead): Good callout. Major cross-team deps: runtime batching/prefix cache (tess), infra prewarm + reserved slots (samir), and compliance items (olivia). Storage eviction semantics may need a schema bump.

tess (Runtime): Runtime plan: add a namespaced prefetch layer + continuous batching adjustments. Can ship a compatibility shim but we need a fallback to a smaller model variant. Rough estimate: 0.5 FTE for 3 sprints to stabilize and run evals on quantized path which may change output quality.

samir (Infra): Infra ask: reserve 8 GPUs for burst/prewarm agents and implement autoscale hooks to attach them. Provisioning + safety testing ~2 weeks. Will create capacity/cost doc with SKU + autoscale playbook. Need finance signoff for reserved pool.

olivia (Security): Quick questions: are we doing KMS namespaced keys or per-tenant HSM? Also need to ensure tenant identifiers are scrubbed from debug logs.
maria (PM): Customer prefers KMS namespacing. @olivia please produce compliance checklist and call out any blockers by Thursday EOD.
olivia (Security): KMS namespacing acceptable. Two immediate items: (1) scrub tenant IDs from debug/trace logs and tokenization metadata, (2) add rotation notes to secrets doc. I'll open a PR with checklist and controls.

jamie (SRE): SLO/runbook: define graceful degradation. Proposed behavior: if burst > capacity, route to fallback smaller model and tag responses as "degraded". Need concrete alert thresholds and an oncall runbook. @deploy-bot can you schedule a canary window?
deploy-bot: Canary window queued: /schedule canary 1974-08-01 09:00 UTC for 48h. Reply :thumbsup: to confirm.
niko (PMM): User comms: prefetch will lower p95/p99 but increase token consumption for some workloads. We'll need a clear pricing/limits note and suggested guardrails for customers.
aj (EngLead): Recap of action owners: tess -> shim + fallback PR by Wed; samir -> capacity plan + reserved GPU cost estimate; olivia -> compliance checklist PR; jamie -> SLOs + runbook draft; maria -> confirm KMS + finalize scope cutlines.

maria (PM): I'll run a 15-min alignment Fri 10:00am to lock scope. Dropping a minimal example config for the runtime shim below. Please comment on any incompatibility.

```
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  tenant_mode: namespaced
  max_prefetch_tokens: 256
  fallback_model: "redwood-small-v1"
  switch_threshold_ms: 80
```

tess (Runtime): That config looks fine. One caveat: only trigger fallback_model when queue_time > switch_threshold_ms; otherwise prefer batching. Need a small eval harness to measure quality regressions and a guardrail for token amplification.
samir (Infra): Will upload the capacity doc later today with SKU, cost, autoscale hooks, and a provisioning checklist. Finance approval required for reserved GPUs; flagging on the roadmap card.

olivia (Security): I'll PR the checklist and a short audit plan (KMS namespace tagging, key rotation schedule, and log scrubbing tests). If anyone needs stricter isolation we can discuss per-tenant KMS accounts but that will increase operational overhead.

jamie (SRE): I'll draft an SLO table and runbook: alerts at 5m sustained error rate increase or queue_time > 300ms for 60s. Rollback steps: disable prefetch toggles, revert to baseline routing, and run traffic to a small canary pool.

maria (PM): Thanks — I'll update the roadmap card and send the calendar invite. If you spot a blocker before Fri, DM me.
